guarantees.claim: When state_sel equals STATE_INIT, state_d is assigned the value of state_init_i.
When state_sel equals STATE_ROUND, state_d is assigned the value of add_round_key_out.
When state_sel equals STATE_CLEAR, state_d is assigned the value of prd_clearing_state_i.
For any other value of state_sel, state_d is assigned prd_clearing_state_i if key_len_i equals AES_256; otherwise state_d is assigned its own previous value, creating a combinational loop.

assumptions.claim: During normal operation, state_sel must be one of STATE_INIT, STATE_ROUND, or STATE_CLEAR when key_len_i != AES_256; otherwise the behaviour relies on the default branch which creates a combinational loop on state_d.
assumptions.risk: A combinational loop may cause state_d to retain a stale or secret previous value, leading to functional deadlock or unintended secret persistence.

uncertain_points.claim: The default branch assigns state_d = state_d (combinational loop) when key_len_i != AES_256, which could cause state to hold previous sensitive data instead of being cleared or initialised if an illegal state_sel occurs. This may violate the intended wipe/clear security property.
uncertain_points.cond: state_sel takes an undefined or illegal value and key_len_i != AES_256
uncertain_points.risk: Secret state (e.g., key schedule or intermediate round values) may persist beyond the intended clearing window, potentially leaking through subsequent side-channel or fault attacks.
